title: The role of taurine in bone metabolism

sections.abstract: Bone metabolism is a dynamic process involving remodeling and rebuilding bone tissue. Important participants in this process include osteoblasts and osteoclasts, which may promote bone formation and bone resorption, respectively. Cumulative evidence suggests that taurine, a sulfur-containing nonessential amino acid, can regulate bone formation, bone resorption, and bone immunity through anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties in bone metabolic diseases. However, the potential mechanisms by which taurine regulates bone metabolism remain unclear. This review focuses on the potential role of taurine in bone metabolic diseases, particularly osteoporosis and rheumatoid arthritis. Moreover, the regulatory mechanisms of taurine on bone formation, bone resorption, and bone immunity are summarized, which provides a theoretical basis for the application of taurine as a therapeutic agent to improve bone metabolic diseases.
sections.introduction:
The development, growth, reconstruction, and healing of the skeletal system are all part of the ongoing process known as bone metabolism. Osteogenesis, or the development of new bone, and resorption, or the destruction of existing bone, are the two main metabolic processes that make bone a dynamic tissue of active cells. 1 The process by which osteoblasts create a bone matrix made of collagen and non-collagenous proteins, such as growth factors and minerals, is known as osteogenesis. Mineralization is the process by which osteoblasts add calcium and phosphate to the bone matrix to create mineralized bone tissue. On the other hand, osteoclast-dominated bone resorption mostly breaks down bone tissue by secreting acids and enzymes that break down the organic matrix and bone minerals. 2 Skeletal reconstruction and calcium ion balance depend heavily on bone formation and resorption. To sustain ideal bone health, a balanced bone metabolism is necessary. Various illnesses that affect bone formation, development, and density maintenance are referred to as bone metabolic disorders. These conditions are usually linked to the processes of bone metabolism. 3 These illnesses may result from an imbalance between bone production and bone resorption. Concerns about bone health are becoming more widespread as the population ages and modern culture changes. The contemporary global context is characterized by a marked trend of population aging, with the prevalence of osteoporosis among individuals over the age of 50 in China exceeding 19.2%, and reaching 32% among those over 65. 4 In addition to lowering patients’ quality of life, bone metabolic diseases like osteoporosis and osteoarthritis place a heavy strain on families and society as a whole. Therefore, researchers are actively searching for natural active substances that can safely and effectively regulate the balance between bone formation and bone resorption. Among these substances, taurine has gradually become a focal point in the field of bone health research due to its wide range of physiological functions and high concentration distribution in bone tissue.

The sulfur-containing amino acid taurine is found in the body in a free state and is not used in the creation of proteins. Nonetheless, it has a close relationship with cysteine and cystine metabolism. The human body contains large amounts of taurine, especially in tissues like bones, muscles, and neurons. It is essential for several physiological functions, such as bone metabolism, calcium homeostasis management, and cytoprotection. Taurine has shown a great deal of promise in the study of bone health in recent years. Through regulating immunological responses and antioxidant mechanisms, taurine not only significantly affects osteoblast activity but also plays a critical role in bone immunity, according to studies. 5 Taurine has been demonstrated to reduce the levels of inhibitors of the Wnt signaling pathway, including Dickkopf-1 (DKK1) and Sclerostin (SOST). These inhibitors typically act by preventing β-catenin stabilization and nuclear translocation, achieved by binding to the Wnt receptor. Inhibition of these antagonists has been demonstrated to result in the deregulation of the Wnt pathway, thereby allowing β-catenin to accumulate in the cytoplasm and enter the nucleus. 6 Furthermore, taurine has been implicated in the regulation of bone growth and development and may influence bone mass by modulating osteoblast function. 7 Additionally, taurine has been shown to protect osteoblasts from reactive oxygen species (ROS)-induced cell death, potentially maintaining osteoblast viability and regulating bone formation by inhibiting scleroprotegerins. 8 It is important to note that the role of taurine extends beyond bone metabolism; it is also implicated in various research areas, including anti-aging, enhancing the effectiveness of cancer treatments, and combating obesity. 9 Taurine has been demonstrated to modulate glucose metabolism and enhance insulin sensitivity. Its dual functions of metabolic regulation and bone protection have rendered it a subject of considerable interdisciplinary research interest. 10 Although taurine supplementation has demonstrated a diverse range of biological functions and potential health benefits in animal studies, our current understanding of the physiological functions and mechanisms of action of taurine remains incomplete. Therefore, further clinical studies are necessary to validate its efficacy and safety in treating human bone metabolic diseases. This paper aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the role of taurine in bone health and to stimulate further research interest in its clinical applications by reviewing recent literature on the regulatory effects of taurine on bone metabolism.
sections.conclusion:
This paper presents a comprehensive review of the significant function of taurine in the regulation of bone metabolism, with particular attention to its potential for the treatment of osteoporosis and RA. Taurine exerts a substantial influence on the equilibrium between bone formation and resorption, promoting osteoblast differentiation and functionality while simultaneously inhibiting osteoclast activity. Furthermore, the antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects of taurine in bone immunomodulation offer novel insights into the potential for combating RA. It is notable that the protective effect of taurine on bone loss and cartilage damage in the RA model, as well as the positive effect on osteoporotic fracture healing, suggests that taurine has significant clinical applications. These findings not only offer new insights into the mechanism of action of taurine in bone health but also provide a scientific foundation for the development of novel therapeutic strategies for bone diseases.

It is recommended that future research should concentrate on a more detailed examination of the mechanism by which taurine regulates osteoblast signaling pathways. In particular, it would be beneficial to investigate the impact of taurine on osteoblasts and osteoclasts through key signaling pathways, such as Wnt/β-catenin and RANKL/OPG. Furthermore, the conduction of extensive clinical trials is imperative to substantiate the efficacy and safety of taurine in diverse populations, thereby facilitating its integration into clinical practice. In light of the necessity to account for individual differences, future treatment strategies must be more personalized. This will entail the development of individualized taurine supplementation plans based on the patient’s genotype, nutritional status, and lifestyle. A combination of genetic testing techniques may be required to predict a patient’s responsiveness to taurine and to adjust treatment regimens accordingly. Furthermore, the role of taurine in the prevention of osteoporosis and RA and the potential for enhancing its endogenous synthesis and utilization through dietary and lifestyle modifications represents a crucial aspect of disease prevention and early intervention. This will not only assist in the reduction of the prevalence of these diseases but will also contribute to a reduction in the associated medical costs and an improvement in the quality of life of the elderly. Concurrently, additional investigation into the mechanism of action and therapeutic efficacy of taurine in other bone metabolic disorders will facilitate the development of a broader range of applications in the domain of bone health. It is anticipated that the findings of these studies will facilitate the development of innovative preventive and therapeutic strategies, which will ultimately provide hope to the growing population of patients with bone metabolic diseases worldwide. These endeavors will facilitate the further utilization of taurine in the management of bone metabolic disorders, offering patients enhanced efficacious and secure treatment alternatives and propelling novel advancements in the domain of bone health investigation.
